title: A Part Sale split off takes the customer's current Part Sales tier
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View', 'Customers — Create & Edit' and 'Part Sales — Create & Edit'.
  • Have a new category for this test, category A, priced by a new matrix for this test, matrix A, with one cost range ($0.00 and up) whose Default rule is Markup % 35.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier A, with a name no other tier uses, whose column in matrix A is % Off 10.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier B, with a name no other tier uses, whose column in matrix A is % Off 20.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, put on tier A for Part Sales in Edit Customer.
  • Have a new Part Sale for this test, Part Sale 1, for customer A, made after customer A's tiers were set, with two parts in category A, cost $100.00 each, priced $121.50 by tier A.
  • Make sure customer A was moved to tier B for Part Sales after Part Sale 1 was made.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so every column of the page shows.
custom_steps:
1. Open Part Sale 1.
  2. Click Split Part Sale in the Part Sale's three-dot menu.
  3. Tick the second part.
  4. Click Split.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part Sale 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The split screen opens as today, listing both parts.

Step 3:

  • The second part is ticked.

Step 4:

  • A new Part Sale opens for customer A with the second part.
  • The moved part reads $108.00, tier B's price ($135.00 × 0.80 = $108.00).
  • The part left on Part Sale 1 still reads $121.50.
